newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Vendex to issue dfl 600 mln Vedior shares.
newsitem.headline: Vendex to issue dfl 600 mln Vedior shares.

text.p: Dutch retail and business services group Vendex International NV said on Tuesday it intended to place shares worth 600 million guilders of its new services group Vedior in the middle of 1997.
Vendex said the placement of the shares, to be listed on the Amsterdam Exchange, would depend on market circumstances.
It said more detailed information on the transaction, the legal and company structure would be made available in a prospectus at a later stage.

Vendex said the shareholders of 'old' Vendex shares would, as soon as possible after the placement, receive the remaining Vedior N.V. shares, which would result in the split-up of the group in two independent, listed companies.

"We expect the split-up to be finalised at the beginning of 1998, depending on the moment at which changes in the law on the split up of legal entities will become valid or the obtaining of an earlier ruling by the Ministry of Finance," Vendex said in a statement.
The legal and other steps needed for the demerger have to be approved at the general shareholders meeting.

On January 6, when the group announced its planned takeover of French temp employment agency BIS SA, Vendex said it intended to demerge its business services division and apply for a separate bourse listing in the first half of 1997.

Vendex chairman Jan-Michiel Hessels said at the time a "substantial" Initial Public Offering (IPO) for the newly created services group Vedior NV would be held once the acquisition of BIS had been finalised.
Vendex earlier on Tuesday announced a 30 percent rise in 1996/97 total net profit to 539 million guilders.
On March 27 BIS posted a 106 million French franc loss for 1996, including a book loss of 215 million francs, down from a profit of 200 million francs the previous year.
When Vendex's take-over bid for BIS expired on March 21, the Dutch company held a 93.4 percent stake.
